mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, which will continue to drive further gains in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite the observed upward trend in the preceding four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in WORKPLACES mobility, particularly if it crosses the -10% threshold, signals a significant return of the workforce to offices, directly boosting weekday retail and recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even if WORKPLACES mobility rises above -10%.

mechanism_narrative: As people progressively spend less time at home, evidenced by decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility, and simultaneously increase their use of public transport, indicated by rising TRANSIT mobility, their opportunities and propensity for out-of-home retail and recreation activities will increase over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to fall and TRANSIT continuing to rise.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, coupled with concurrent increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, suggests an ongoing policy of easing movement restrictions, which will continue to free up people for retail and recreation activities over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, even if RESIDENTIAL continues to fall and WORKPLACES/TRANSIT continue to rise.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates an immediate shift in daily routines away from home, directly translating to increased out-of-home activities like retail and recreation in the very next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next 7 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility falling by more than 1 point week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent recovery in TRANSIT station visits over the past four weeks reflects increasing public confidence and necessity for out-of-home movement, which will continue to support growth in retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, despite TRANSIT mobility continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: Even with relatively stable GROCERY_PHARM visits, the increasing WORKPLACES mobility suggests a return to more complex daily routines where people combine work commutes with other errands and leisure, thereby boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise and GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable.

mechanism_narrative: If the current positive trend in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility reverses, with either falling by more than 5 points week-on-week, it would signal a re-imposition of restrictions or a new wave of public caution, leading to a decline in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES or TRANSIT falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, even if WORKPLACES or TRANSIT falls by more than 5 points week-on-week.
